title: Investor Awareness: Fraud Red Flags and Protection Guidelines

sections.content: SEBI cautions investors against AI-manipulated videos (deepfakes) and voice clones of senior government officials, corporate executives, or reputed analysts endorsing private investment schemes or algorithmic software. Genuine regulators and market leaders never promote private trading software or specific investment schemes.
key_takeaways: AI deepfakes impersonating regulators and corporate leaders
Regulators never endorse private apps or investment schemes

sections.section_title: Unregistered Financial Influencers and Telegram Tipsters
sections.content: Offering investment advice, research analyst reports, or portfolio management services without valid SEBI registration is illegal under SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013. Unregistered entities operating across Telegram, YouTube, and WhatsApp frequently execute pump-and-dump manipulations to offload shares onto retail followers.
key_takeaways: Advising without SEBI registration is illegal
Unregistered social media groups frequently conduct pump-and-dump schemes

sections.section_title: OTP Confidentiality and Prohibition of Remote-Access Software
sections.content: Investors must never share One-Time Passwords (OTPs), PINs, or demat account login credentials under any circumstance. Legitimate stock exchanges and brokers will never ask users to install screen-sharing or remote desktop tools (e.g., AnyDesk, TeamViewer) to resolve trading or KYC issues.
key_takeaways: Never share OTPs, PINs, or trading passwords
Never install remote screen-sharing tools for broker or KYC support

sections.section_title: Prohibition of Assured and Guaranteed Returns
sections.content: Under SEBI regulations, no registered intermediary or collective scheme is permitted to promise fixed or guaranteed returns in equity and derivative markets. Any solicitation promising zero-risk, assured daily/weekly interest, or guaranteed capital doubling is a cardinal indicator of fraud.
key_takeaways: Guaranteed returns in securities markets are prohibited by SEBI
Zero-risk claims are cardinal indicators of investment fraud
